newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cadbury confident about second half.
newsitem.headline: Cadbury confident about second half.

text.p: International beverage and confectionery group Cadbury Schweppes Plc said on Wednesday it was confident about its second half performance after achieving positive results from its two key divisions in the first half of 1997.
The company said its beverages division achieved a 29 percent rise in first half trading profit while the confectionery division achieved a three percent rise.
The strength of sterling reduced earnings from the beverages division by 11 million stg and by five million for the confectionery division.

"Sales and market shares of both streams benefited from the introduction of new products, the continued international expansion of existing brands and higher levels of marketing investment," the company said in its review of operations.

"Cadbury Schweppes has achieved positive results in both business streams in the first half of 1997, with confectionery gaining momentum after the slow start in some markets, to which I referred at the AGM in May," chairman Sir Dominic Cadbury said in a statement accompanying the first half results.
"We look forward to the second half of the year with confidence," he said.
The company's results were sent to the Australian Stock Exchange, where it is listed, by its local offshoot, Cadbury Schweppes Australia Ltd.

The chairman said a direct comparison of the latest results with the 1996 first half was affected by the sale of the 51 percent stake in Coca-Cola & Schweppes Beverages Ltd (CCSB) in February this year, the strength of sterling and the absence of major restructuring costs in the latest period.
"After adjusting for these items, sales and profit before tax increased by five percent and 10 percent respectively," he said.
The CCSB sale led to pre-tax gain of 417 million stg in the latest period, representing a net gain of 332 milln stg and contributing to a 45 percent fall in net borrowings to 882 million stg.

Earnings before tax and gains from disposals rose to 236 million stg in the six months to June 14 from 231 million stg a year earlier, representing a two percent rise on an "actual currency basis" and a rise of nine percent on a "constant currency basis".
Turnover from continuing operations fell to 1.837 billion stg from 1.894 billion stg, a rise of five percent on a constant currency basis.
The company said the beverages division, which now excludes CCSB, achieved a three percent rise in sales from continuing operations after excluding restructuring costs and at constant exchange rates.
Profits from continuing operations rose by six percent on the same basis, it said, without providing specific figures for the results of each division.

"Trading profit benefited from the absence of restructuring costs in the first half 1997 and grew by 29 percent, despite the 11 million stg negative effect of the strength of sterling," the company said of the beverage unit's performance.
"Trading margin grew to over 16 percent and marketing investment grew by nine percent."

U.S. soft drink volume rose by 0.9 percent in the latest six months. Dr Pepper volumes rose by 4.3 percent while the performance of 7-UP and other brands fell although the decline eased in the second quarter.
The company said its confectionery division achieved higher sales, profits and market share in the United Kingdom but losses continued from operations in China and Russia.
"Sales for the first half of 1997 were level with those of 1996 and trading profit grew by three percent at constant exchange rates," it said of the division's performance.
"Sales and profits were reduced by 63 million stg and five million stg respectively, because of the strength of sterling.
"Trading margin improved after adjusting for 'greenfield' investments in Russia and China," it said.
-- Sydney Newroom 61-2 9373-1800
